Struct ringcask::RingBuffer

source
pub struct RingBuffer<T> { /* private fields */ }
Expand description

A fixed-capacity, single-producer ring buffer backed by a boxed slice.

Writes never allocate after construction, which makes the buffer suitable for audio callbacks, interrupt handlers, and other places where a pause for the allocator is not acceptable. When the buffer is full, push returns the rejected value instead of overwriting the oldest one.

§Examples

use ringcask::RingBuffer;

let mut rb = RingBuffer::with_capacity(2);
assert!(rb.push(1).is_ok());
assert!(rb.push(2).is_ok());
assert_eq!(rb.push(3), Err(3));
assert_eq!(rb.pop(), Some(1));

§Capacity

The capacity is fixed at construction time and is never rounded up, so a buffer created with a capacity of five holds exactly five items. Internally, one index is reserved to tell a full buffer from an empty one, but that slot is allocated separately and does not reduce the usable capacity.

§Panics

Creating a buffer with a capacity of zero panics, because a buffer that can hold nothing is almost always a logic error. If you need an empty placeholder, wrap the buffer in an Option instead.
